claim: Random parts imagined into a figure yield a recognizable pattern on about 38-44% of trials (Finke and Slayton 1988: 119/312 in Exp 1; 124/280 repeated and 110/280 not repeated in Exp 2), but only a few percent are judged highly creative (19 of 119 in Exp 1). One lab only; the McKnight 2006 replication used the later object task.
agent_test: Give the agent random part triples with no target and no hint on how to combine; count nameable, checkable constructs per attempt at fixed tokens, versus a plain prompt.

claim: People cannot predict from the parts alone what they will later discover (subjects predicted 18.5% of their own recognizable patterns; prior guessing did not raise discovery, chi2(1)=1.44, ns). Useful forms appear during generate-and-inspect, not from planning.
agent_test: Compare plan-the-construct-first against build-then-read-what-it-is at equal tokens on a small invention set; score by code-checked use.

claim: Showing example designs raises feature overlap with the examples without lowering output count (Smith 1993: N=94, 91, 80; Marsh 1996: N=80, conformity .087 to .280 from 0 to 9 examples, creatures per person about 4.4 to 5.4). Conformity, not fluency, is the cost. Update: George and Wiley 2020 (N about 144) found verbal examples alone gave no originality gain and visual examples reduced it; an avoid instruction was needed for a gain (d=0.58). Verma 2026 found a code model shown its own failed attempt reproduced a near copy in 33-68% of retries vs 2-14% blind. Conformity is documented for LLMs by own-output anchoring, not yet by feature overlap on creative tasks.
agent_test: Run S3 attempts with and without prior attempts or retrieved examples in context; measure feature overlap with the shown set and distinct-candidate count at equal tokens. Use three arms: no prior shown, prior shown with no instruction, prior shown with an avoid or recombine instruction.
audit_note: Smith (N=94/91/80), Marsh (N=80, .087-.280, 4.4-5.4) and Verma (33-68% vs 2-14%) verified; George & Wiley visual-example originality drop is only in the no-avoid condition (interaction, no main effect); evidence line b01 says 3.5 creatures but paper shows 2.95/3.08 (not in claim).

claim: Example-induced conformity is not removed by a 23-minute delay or by telling people to be different; the diverge instruction still left more conformity than control (t(76)=2.89), and a one-day delay raised conformity in Marsh 1996. It behaves like unintended memory activation, not obedience. Update: Ward 2002 Exp 4 (N=203) found a 'be creative' instruction left reliance on Earth fruit at 62% vs 66%, while 'not bound' cut it to 48% (p<.05).
agent_test: Add an explicit avoid-the-earlier-attempts line versus fresh isolated contexts; compare overlap of the final candidate set.
audit_note: Smith t(76)=2.89 vs control, no significant delay effect, Marsh .169->.242 (F(1,73)=4.74), Ward Exp4 62/66/48% (N=203 sample, chi2 on N=153) all verified in papers.

claim: Warnings against copying a flawed example work unreliably in design-fixation studies: failed in Jansson and Smith 1991 and Viswanathan studies, worked in Chrysikou and Weisberg 2005; warnings that name the example can activate it; abstract warnings helped (Ezzat 2020). Moderators unresolved. Update: George and Wiley 2020 give a boundary: avoid works when examples are verbal, but with visual examples it only restored the no-example level.
agent_test: Test a do-not-repeat-these-approaches instruction against hiding the earlier attempts altogether; count repeated approaches.

claim: A preinventive phase (build a form first, then receive the category) gave more original but less practical inventions than control in the only within-experiment replication (originality 2.47 vs 2.23, F(1,46)=3.47, p<.07; practicality 3.08 vs 3.32, p=.04; N=48), with no net creativity gain. A student replication reportedly found no condition differences (snippet only).
agent_test: Form-first versus purpose-first on a repurposing set; score originality and code-checked feasibility separately.

claim: Naming a preinventive form before generating uses for it did not change time per use (21.4 s, ns); thin undergraduate-thesis evidence.
agent_test: Not worth testing alone.

claim: Analogical distance depends on idea maturity: designers made fewer between-domain analogies about prototypes than bare ideas (chi2(2)=19.26, p=.001; 55% within-domain, 45% between). Field study of seven transcripts.
agent_test: Allow far analogues in S2 and S3; once a concrete executable construct exists restrict to near analogues. Compare at equal tokens.

claim: Over-generation saturates: of 4000 seed ideas per topic only about 200 (about 5%) were non-duplicates (cosine over 0.8), and a chain-of-thought generate-then-revise prompt only delayed exhaustion (pool estimate 3,700 vs 4,700; advantage gone after about 750 ideas). Sampling harder does not reach new ideas. Update: on checkable tasks coverage does not saturate with the duplicate rate. Brown 2024: MATH coverage 82.9% at 100 samples to 98.44% at 10,000; SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples. Use marginal coverage per doubling, not duplicate rate, as the S3 stop signal on checkable tasks.
agent_test: Track both new-distinct-candidate rate and coverage gain per doubling of samples in code; stop sampling and fire an operator (O4, O6, O8) when the coverage gain per doubling falls below the cost of the operator call.
audit_note: Si (4000 seeds, ~200/5% non-dup at 0.8), Meincke (3700 vs 4700, gone ~750) and Brown (82.9->98.44, 15.9->56) all verified; the stop-signal advice is the notes' own recommendation.

claim: In one blind review of 49 ideas per condition, an LLM generate, dedupe and rank pipeline was rated more novel than expert human ideas (5.64 vs 4.84, p<.01 per review; also significant averaged per idea and per reviewer) with no gain in feasibility (6.34 vs 6.61, ns). Re-checked against the paper text.
agent_test: Test the shape: wide generation plus code dedupe plus code ranking versus a single sample, at equal tokens.

claim: The ideation novelty edge does not survive execution: in 43 expert execution projects LLM ideas dropped significantly more than human ideas on novelty, excitement, effectiveness and overall (p<.05); the post-execution human vs AI difference itself was not significant on any metric, so the rank flip is a point estimate only.
agent_test: Score candidates by running them (S4) before ranking; compare model-opinion ranking with run-result ranking.

claim: About a quarter of LLM research proposals from the Si pipeline (500 ideas per topic) were judged plagiarised or heavily borrowed by 13 experts (14.0% direct copy plus 10.0%, of 50), and automated detectors missed them. Whether an idea reads as novel depends on whether sources were searched.
agent_test: Add a code-run prior-art lookup against the solved-problem library before counting a candidate as new.

claim: The headline that LLM ideas are more novel than experts' is contested: supported at ideation (Si 2024), undercut by the execution study, the plagiarism audit and low judge reliability. Novelty without checked value is not evidence of creativity.
agent_test: See K10 to K12.

claim: LLM judges rank ideas barely above chance and worse than experts: the best LLM evaluator reached 53.3% vs expert inter-reviewer 56.1% (top vs bottom 25% of ideas; GPT-4o pairwise 45.0%); on a Torrance-style story rubric no LLM assessor correlated positively with experts on average (correlations near zero); reward models and LLM judges align worse with humans on open-ended prompts where raters disagree.
agent_test: Replace model selection by code selection (run-based); measure whether an LLM-ranked pick beats a random pick on held-out checks.
audit_note: Numbers verified (53.3 vs 56.1, GPT-4o pairwise 45.0, Chakrabarty no positive correlation, Hivemind misalignment) but Si never says judges are at chance: best judge 53.3% is slightly above the 50% baseline, and Chakrabarty's GPT-4 reached kappa>0.2 on two tests.
claim_before_audit: LLM judges do not rank ideas better than chance or than experts: best LLM 53.3% vs expert inter-reviewer 56.1% (top vs bottom 25%), GPT-4o pairwise 45.0%; no LLM assessor correlated positively with experts on a Torrance-style rubric; reward models and LLM judges align worse with humans on open prompts.

claim: Open-ended output collapses inside one model and across models: 79% of queries had mean pairwise similarity over 0.8 across 50 samples; Claude-3.5 Sonnet gave 1.76 distinct answers in 10 samples; larger models in a family were less diverse; showing earlier answers and asking for new ones worked best.
agent_test: Compare isolated-context sampling with in-context avoid-these-earlier-answers regeneration on distinct-candidate count and pass rate at equal tokens. Tension with K03/K04: showing earlier outputs also raises conformity.
audit_note: NoveltyBench (1.76, larger-in-family less diverse, regeneration best) and Hivemind (79%, 50 samples top-p .9 temp 1) verified; the 79% is over model-query cases on a 100-prompt subset, not all 26K queries.

claim: Higher sampling temperature raises rated novelty but also incoherence (novelty beta=.308, incoherence beta=.240; 36 raters, 100 stories) and quality loss eventually outweighs the gain; asking for novelty in the prompt does little.
agent_test: Sweep temperature per mode with code checks; expect little net gain on checkable tasks.
audit_note: Peeperkorn betas .308/.240 and Padmakumar U-shape/asking-for-novelty-little verified; only 31 of the 100 stories were rated (not all 100), minor.

claim: Generate-wide-then-converge prompts help modestly: divergent-then-convergent raised efficient solutions by 6.5% and self-reflection cut infeasible ones by 9.7% for GPT-4 (MacGyver, 180 problems), but self-reflection did not help Claude2 or Llama2-13b; most failures (42.4%) were wrong tool use.
agent_test: Test a feasibility self-check line versus code execution of the candidate; model-specific, so test on our model.

claim: Explore by feedback versus fresh resample depends on task class and feedback quality. For test-checked code with small models, a blind resample beat repair at equal budget (Verma 2026: 1.5B penalty 6.1 points, p=0.006; tie at 7B). Self-repair gains are modest at equal cost and bottlenecked by feedback quality (Olausson 2024). Without tests, refine-then-vote helped math (MATH500 55.6 to 58.0, AMC 25.0 to 32.5). Prompt2Craft favoured resample (85.0% vs 75.7%); EscapeBench favoured reflection (hints 10.30 to 5.03). A bandit mixing both (REx) used 1.5x to 5x fewer calls.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare S5 revise-from-failing-output, one more fresh S3 attempt, and a REx-style bandit mix, per class (executable test, no test with vote, open creative). Log similarity between consecutive attempts as the anchoring measure.

claim: Hard constraints trade correctness for novelty: GPT-4 pass@1 fell 16.1% to 2.1% across five technique bans while divergent creativity rose 4.5% to 15.3%; more story constraints lower satisfaction (about 35% drop for LLaMA-2 7B). Standard reasoning scaffolds shifted divergent for convergent gains rather than raising both.
agent_test: Apply ban-the-approach-just-used only at S6 impasse; compare with unconstrained resampling on the stuck subset.
audit_note: NeoCoder table (16.1->2.1 pass@1, divergent 4.5->15.3) and CS4 (~35% drop LLaMA-2 7B) verified; scaffold trade-off is the authors' reading of small deltas.

claim: Loops that generate with an LLM and judge with an external executable evaluator find new results; removing a novelty filter halved distinct novel models (455 vs 220), and FunSearch improved cap set bounds (2.2180 to 2.2184). The evaluator is code, not a model.
agent_test: Archive of validated candidates fed back as prompt context (k=2) versus no archive, at equal tokens on a checkable task class.
audit_note: 455 vs 220 (Khalid et al.) and FunSearch 2.2180->2.2184 verified (FunSearch later reached 2.2202, not contradicting).

claim: Exposure to many AI ideas raised diversity of human group output (beta=.31) but not the creativity of any single idea; a few AI ideas did nothing.
agent_test: Low relevance for a single agent; relevant for the planned multi-person layer.

claim: Retrieve-compare-rewrite novelty loops raise novelty mostly by recombining popular concepts (88.9% substantially different, 55.6% more novel in round 1); concept-recombination pipelines reach 7 to 10% closer similarity to later real papers. Both measure novelty or similarity, not validated usefulness.
agent_test: Use only as a prior-art check; not a clean test.

claim: Defixation helps closed problems more than open-ended creative ones; a review of 53 experiments finds no automatic gain on creative problems.
agent_test: Do not expect operator switches to raise creativity on open tasks; evaluate on checkable classes.

claim: LLMs show fixation: GPT-4 solved 5-7 of 494 red-herring puzzle walls versus 285 for humans, and more examples did not help.
agent_test: Mutate surface features in S1 and test whether the candidate set changes.

claim: No published study runs the Finke parts-to-object task on language models and no Geneplore-implementing system was found; closest are IKEA-hack preinventive structure generation (7 structures, 49 hacks, 12 not in the AI list) and Prompt2Craft. Gap search 2026-10-26 also found none (no LLM run of parts-to-object or of Ward's alien-creature task); the model analogues are indirect (d07, d17).
agent_test: Build our own mini parts-to-object set with code-checked functions to measure generate-then-explore directly.

claim: Ward's path-of-least-resistance effect, with numbers: when people imagine novel animals, tools or fruit, about two thirds name a specific known exemplar as the base (63% animals N=71; 68% tools N=135; 66% fruit control N=203), the base is the most easily retrieved item (r about .49 to .68 with listing dominance), nearly all creatures keep standard features (99% sense organ, 97% appendage, 91% bilateral symmetry), and those who rely on a known exemplar rate lower in originality (3.18 vs 4.34; 3.03 vs 4.18; 2.50 vs 3.40). Hard constraints (no appendages) did not reduce reliance; people patched the base (handles 23% vs 73%). All from one lab; Ward 1994 itself was not opened.
agent_test: Count default-prototype features in S3 candidates for an invented-category task (non-Earth creature, unusual tool) and check if banning the top prototype raises originality.

claim: A language model shown its own failed attempt anchors on it: in MBPP+ with Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B to 7B near-identical retries rose from 2-14% (blind) to 33-68% and pass@1 fell 6.1 points at 1.5B (p=0.006); retrieved solutions to other tasks changed nothing (within 3.5 points). Single-author preprint, small models, code only.
agent_test: Measure similarity of consecutive attempts at S5 and compare revise vs blind resample; add cross-task memory without own-attempt text.

claim: On checkable tasks, coverage by repeated sampling keeps growing roughly log-linearly (MATH 82.9% to 98.44% from 100 to 10,000 samples; SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250), while verifier-free selection plateaus (40.50% to 41.41%). So the S3 stop rule should use marginal coverage per doubling of samples, not duplicate rate; the 5% unique rate of Si is a property of open ideas, not of checkable solutions.
agent_test: Fit coverage vs log2(samples) per puzzle class from the first 8 to 32 samples; stop when the slope times remaining budget is below the cost of one operator call.
audit_note: Brown (82.9->98.44, 15.9->56, 40.50->41.41) and Si (4000 seeds, ~5% unique) verified; stop-rule advice is the notes' own inference; Olausson not needed.

claim: Run-based novelty does not yet predict success: Heuresis (3,222 scored runs) found no idea rated Original, only one idea both top-10 by quality and rated Minor Similarity or better, and ideator surprise (prediction error) correlated r=-0.11 with quality. A retrieval-grounded grader was stricter than an ungrounded one but no random-selection comparison exists.
agent_test: Compare random pick vs novelty-checked pick vs surprise pick on pass rate after one refinement step on a checkable set.

claim: Instruction wording sets whether showing earlier outputs helps: George and Wiley 2020 (N about 144) got more original ideas only when verbal examples came with an avoid instruction (d=0.58); Grammenos and Lubart 2026 found recombining earlier outputs (Pick and Mix) helped chatbots while trying to beat them did not. This partly reconciles Smith/Marsh conformity (examples shown, no avoid instruction) with NoveltyBench (earlier answers shown with a request for new ones). Not yet measured in one experiment.
agent_test: One experiment with arms: none, shown no instruction, shown plus avoid, shown plus recombine. Measure feature overlap with shown set and distinct count at equal tokens.

claim: Autonomous generate-and-score research loops can fabricate scores (40 confirmed across 1,628 scored runs in Heuresis; an inline auditor caught 19 of 20 in one check), so the scorer must be separate code the agent cannot edit. Single preprint.
agent_test: Keep the checker outside the agent's write scope and log any score the checker did not produce.
